articles.title: 专访英国经济学家罗思义：与中国合作才是欧洲合理的选择
articles.highlight: 欧洲的经济问题不是中国制造的问题，当政府部门一些人不断推动保护主义时，欧洲的行业主体却开始反对保护主义。
articles.summary: 文章报道，近期欧洲对华贸易保护主义持续抬头，但今年参加进博会的欧洲企业数量达到上千家，欧洲学界及产业界也纷纷发声反对贸易保护主义。英国经济学家罗思义认为，欧洲的经济问题并非源于中国制造，政府层面推动保护主义时，欧洲行业主体却在反对保护主义。这有助于观察欧洲对华政策表态与产业界实际选择之间的分化。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键看点在于，欧洲政治层面的保护主义升温，并不等于企业界愿意放弃与中国的合作。

articles.title: Umberto Eco’s Antilibrary: Why Unread Books Are More Valuable to Our Lives than Read Ones
articles.highlight: 在一个把知识当作让我们在等级秩序中攀升的装饰的文化里，如何成为一个“反学者”。
articles.summary: 文章围绕艾柯的“反图书馆”概念，讨论未读之书为何可能比已读之书对生活更有价值。它进一步追问：在一个把知识当作阶层攀升装饰的文化里，人如何成为“反学者”。这值得读，因为它促使人重新思考阅读与知识的意义，而不只把它们当作身份展示。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启发：把知识当装饰会让人追逐身份排序；保留大量未读之书，可提醒自己未知仍大、学习不该止于展示。
articles.sourceExcerpt: How to become an "antischolar" in a culture that treats knowledge as "an ornament that allows us to rise in the pecking order."

en.highlight: How to become an "antischolar" in a culture that treats knowledge as "an ornament that allows us to rise in the pecking order."
en.summary: The piece uses Umberto Eco's idea of the "antilibrary" to ask why unread books may matter more to our lives than read ones. It also asks how to become an "antischolar" in a culture that treats knowledge as an ornament for climbing the pecking order. articles.title: nano-muse/nanoMuse
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + Community signal
articles.summary: 这个 GitHub 项目提出开源个人代理，覆盖手机、电脑和浏览器，把手机屏幕与电脑作为“手”来执行任务。它强调有独立名称与外观、应用关闭后仍可工作、记住用户，并在不可逆操作前征求确认。值得关注的是它试图把跨设备个人代理做成可部署的开源产品，而不只是单点 AI 功能。
articles.failureAnalysis: 最大风险在工程与信任：跨 Android、iOS、桌面和浏览器持续运行，受后台限制、耗电、权限和系统沙箱约束，稳定执行并不容易。它要接触屏幕、文件和设备操作，一旦误操作或数据泄露，用户信任成本很高；开源还带来安全审计与滥用治理压力。需求侧也要验证用户是否愿意把跨设备日常任务交给一个统一代理，而不是继续用现成助理和自动化工具。
articles.highlight: 一个有名有貌的代理，能做事、在应用关闭后继续工作、记住你，并在不可逆操作前先询问。
articles.sourceExcerpt: GitHub repository with 3293 stars and recent public activity. Description: nanoMuse: an open-source personal agent for every device you own. One agent with a name and a look of its own that does things, keeps working while the app is closed, remembers you, and asks before anything you cannot undo.

en.highlight: One agent with a name and a look of its own that does things, keeps working while the app is closed, remembers you, and asks before anything you cannot undo.
en.summary: This GitHub project presents an open-source personal agent spanning Android, iPhone/iPad, Windows/macOS/Linux, and the browser, using the phone screen and computer as its hands. It emphasizes a named, distinct-looking agent that keeps working while the app is closed, remembers the user, and asks before irreversible actions. It is worth reading as an attempt to turn cross-device personal agents into a deployable open-source product rather than a single AI feature.
en.failureAnalysis: The main risks are engineering and trust: always-on cross-device execution faces background limits, battery use, permissions, and sandboxing, while screen/file access makes mistakes and data exposure costly. It also needs validation that users will delegate everyday cross-device tasks to one agent instead of existing assistants and automation tools.
en.title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device
